title: English Vocabulary 4 · Units 79–80
description: Advanced research-writing vocabulary, interpretation of evidence, precision in presenting academic arguments, categorisation, cohesion and text structure.
sourceNotice: Prepared for personal study based on the user-provided Advanced third edition. Vocabulary and constructions were selected from the study pages, exercises and answer key; translations, sentences and usage notes were independently written without reproducing textbook exercises or extended source passages.

audit.scope: Unit 79 sections A–C and exercises 79.1–79.5; Unit 80 sections A–C, Common mistakes and exercises 80.1–80.4; corresponding answer-key entries.
audit.pronunciation: Selected short single-word entries have broad British IPA where confident. Extended expressions have blank IPA rather than unverified connected-speech transcriptions.
audit.languagePolicy: All learner-facing and metadata language is English, except Brazilian Portuguese translations in pt fields.
audit.reviewMethod: Checked unit study pages, facing exercises and corresponding answer-key entries. Original sentences and meaning notes underwent editorial review; JSON fields, types, IDs, provenance and audio-target handling were checked programmatically against the canonical reference.
audit.limitations: No recorded audio is bundled. App import, browser TTS and pronunciation recognition were not run. Word audio uses item word or a brief speechText target where the displayed phrase is open-ended.

units.title: Unit 79 — Academic writing: making sense
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 79. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
units.category: Academic writing · argument, evidence and precision
learningObjectives: Distinguish advocating, deducing, inferring, complementing and overlapping when discussing research.
Evaluate academic works as empirical, authoritative, ambiguous, coherent or comprehensive.
Describe statistical patterns without confusing incidence, predominance and deviation.
Use formal academic verbs and linkers with accurate meanings, register and sentence structure.

sectionsChecked: A · Presenting arguments and commenting on others’ work
B · Talking about figures and processes
C · Words typically used in academic contexts
Exercises 79.1–79.5 and the corresponding answer key

items.pt: defender; recomendar publicamente uma ideia ou medida
items.example: The researchers advocate stricter procedures for documenting experimental failures.
items.note: Advocate an approach or advocate doing something means argue in favour of it, not merely describe it.

items.pt: deduzir logicamente a partir de fatos conhecidos
items.example: From the timing data, we can deduce that the system entered its idle state before the fault occurred.
items.note: Deduce a conclusion from known facts through a process of reasoning; compare infer.

items.pt: inferir; concluir indiretamente a partir de indícios
items.example: We may infer from the interview transcripts that several participants were reluctant to disagree.
items.note: Infer something from evidence is to reach an indirect conclusion; the writer or listener infers.

items.pt: inferir a partir das evidências
items.example: It is premature to infer from the evidence that the intervention improves long-term outcomes.
items.note: In academic prose, distinguish inference from direct observation or a definitively proven finding.

items.pt: complementar; combinar-se de modo a aumentar a eficácia
items.example: The laboratory measurements complement the simulation results by revealing effects the model overlooks.
items.note: Complement with e means enhance or complete something; not compliment, meaning praise.

items.pt: sobrepor-se parcialmente; ter partes em comum
items.example: The two studies overlap in their treatment of social mobility but differ in methodology.
items.note: Research can overlap in subject matter without being identical; often followed by with.

items.pt: confiável por sua especialização; de referência
items.example: Her authoritative survey of the literature is widely cited in subsequent studies.
items.note: An authoritative work is thorough and produced by a recognised expert; it is not necessarily beyond criticism.

items.pt: empírico; fundamentado na observação ou em dados
items.example: The theoretical framework was tested against empirical data from three independent laboratories.
items.note: Empirical research relies on observation or measurement rather than theory alone.

items.pt: ambíguo; aberto a mais de uma interpretação
items.example: The wording of the questionnaire was ambiguous, making the responses difficult to interpret.
items.note: Ambiguous evidence or language supports more than one interpretation; not simply inaccurate.

items.pt: coerente; estruturado de forma lógica
items.example: The discussion presents a coherent argument connecting the hypothesis to the observed findings.
items.note: A coherent argument follows logically and can be understood as a unified whole.

items.pt: abrangente; que cobre todos os aspectos relevantes
items.example: The review provides a comprehensive account of the available detection methods.
items.note: Comprehensive emphasises breadth of coverage; it does not necessarily mean flawless.

items.pt: pesquisas complementares
items.example: The teams conducted complementary research using different populations and measurement techniques.
items.note: An independent application of the unit’s complement concept; complementary does not mean identical.

items.pt: arbitrário; definido sem critério sistemático ou justificativa em dados
items.example: The authors acknowledged that the initial cut-off value was arbitrary.
items.note: An arbitrary choice reflects chance or preference instead of a defensible rule or evidence.

items.pt: desviar-se do padrão; afastar-se do comportamento habitual
items.example: The measurements deviate from the norm only under unusually high temperatures.
items.note: Deviate from means differ from an established expectation or standard; the difference can be in either direction.

items.pt: distorcer o panorama; transmitir uma impressão enganosa
items.example: Reporting only the strongest results would distort the picture of the intervention’s effectiveness.
items.note: An idiomatic research expression for misrepresenting the overall evidence.

items.pt: incidência; frequência de ocorrência
items.example: The incidence of reporting errors fell after the new review procedure was introduced.
items.note: Incidence here is how often something occurs; it is not the severity of each individual event.

items.pt: a incidência de; a frequência de ocorrência de
items.example: The study measured the incidence of equipment failures over a five-year period.
items.note: Use the incidence of an event or condition, not the incidence for in this meaning.

items.pt: predominante; mais frequente ou numeroso
items.example: In this sample, the predominant reason for withdrawal was lack of time.
items.note: Predominant describes the most common or numerically largest category, not necessarily a majority.

items.pt: em sequência; em uma ordem determinada
items.example: The trial phases must be conducted in sequence to avoid contaminating the results.
items.note: Describes ordered steps; sequentially is the related adverb.

items.pt: generalizado; disseminado por muitos lugares ou pessoas
items.example: The authors found widespread support for the policy across different age groups.
items.note: Widespread describes broad distribution or prevalence, not necessarily great intensity.

items.pt: preocupação generalizada
items.example: The data breach caused widespread concern among researchers who shared sensitive information.
items.note: A common academic collocation for a reaction present across many people or groups.

items.pt: acrescentar ao final; anexar
items.section: C · Academic vocabulary and linking expressions
items.example: The authors appended the detailed coding scheme to the published report.
items.note: Append a document or detail to something, usually at the end; more formal than add.

items.pt: conceber; formular uma ideia ou teoria
items.section: C · Academic vocabulary and linking expressions
items.example: The research programme was conceived during a discussion of the limitations of existing models.
items.note: Conceive a project or theory means formulate it as an idea before implementing it.

items.pt: contradizer; contrariar conclusões ou afirmações
items.section: C · Academic vocabulary and linking expressions
items.example: The new observations contradict the assumptions underlying the original proposal.
items.note: Contradict is stronger than merely differ from; it signals incompatibility with a claim.

items.pt: demonstrar; evidenciar com argumentos ou resultados
items.section: C · Academic vocabulary and linking expressions
items.example: The results demonstrate a measurable reduction in energy consumption.
items.note: In research writing, demonstrate typically claims stronger evidential support than suggest.

items.pt: indicar; sugerir que os dados apontam para algo
items.section: C · Academic vocabulary and linking expressions
items.example: The preliminary findings indicate a possible relationship between the two variables.
items.note: Indicate can present evidence cautiously without implying conclusive proof.

items.pt: denotar; representar por meio de um símbolo ou termo
items.section: C · Academic vocabulary and linking expressions
items.example: In the proposed notation, the symbol lambda denotes the arrival rate.
items.note: Use denote when a symbol, term or mark stands for a specific concept.

items.pt: negar; anular a validade ou o efeito de
items.section: C · Academic vocabulary and linking expressions
items.example: These additional findings do not negate the earlier evidence; they refine its interpretation.
items.note: Negate suggests cancelling, invalidating or making something ineffective.

items.pt: perceber; interpretar ou compreender sob certa perspectiva
items.section: C · Academic vocabulary and linking expressions
items.example: Some interviewees perceived the new procedure as an unnecessary restriction.
items.note: Perceive often reports someone’s understanding or impression, which may be subjective.

items.pt: refletir sobre; analisar de modo ponderado
items.section: C · Academic vocabulary and linking expressions
items.example: The final chapter reflects upon the ethical implications of the research.
items.note: A formal alternative to think about when examining ideas or past developments.

items.pt: residir em; estar localizado em ou pertencer a
items.section: C · Academic vocabulary and linking expressions
items.example: The explanation may reside in differences between the two sampling strategies.
items.note: Formal: a fact, quality or explanation can reside in something, not just a person in a place.

items.pt: desencadear; provocar o início de um processo
items.section: C · Academic vocabulary and linking expressions
items.example: The unexpected signal triggered a series of automated safety checks.
items.note: Trigger emphasises initiating a reaction or process rather than describing its entire development.

items.pt: utilizar; empregar para um objetivo específico
items.section: C · Academic vocabulary and linking expressions
items.example: The investigators utilised archival records to reconstruct the sequence of events.
items.note: Formal alternative to use; plain use is often clearer when extra formality is unnecessary.

items.pt: um exemplo de; um caso de
items.section: C · Academic vocabulary and linking expressions
items.example: The observed anomaly is an instance of a broader pattern reported in the literature.
items.note: Formal alternative to an example of, typically in analytical prose.

items.pt: o inverso; a proposição oposta
items.section: C · Academic vocabulary and linking expressions
items.example: Some studies suggest that larger teams are more productive, but our findings indicate the converse.
items.note: The converse refers to the reverse relationship or opposite assertion.

items.pt: crucial; decisivo; de importância fundamental
items.section: C · Academic vocabulary and linking expressions
items.example: Reliable calibration is crucial to the validity of these measurements.
items.note: A strong academic alternative to very important; often followed by to or for.

items.pt: não obstante; apesar disso
items.section: C · Academic vocabulary and linking expressions
items.example: The sample was relatively small; notwithstanding, the findings warrant further investigation.
items.note: Formal concessive connector meaning nevertheless or despite this; punctuation and position vary.

items.pt: um tanto; relativamente; em certa medida
items.section: C · Academic vocabulary and linking expressions
items.example: The second model produced somewhat different estimates from the first.
items.note: A measured modifier that reduces the force of an adjective or comparison.

items.pt: dessa forma; por esse meio; consequentemente
items.section: C · Academic vocabulary and linking expressions
items.example: The revision reduced unnecessary processing, thereby improving the system’s efficiency.
items.note: Thereby links an action to the consequence or means it creates; often followed by an -ing clause.

items.pt: pelo qual; por meio do qual; mediante o qual
items.section: C · Academic vocabulary and linking expressions
items.example: The team devised a protocol whereby participants could withdraw their data securely.
items.note: Whereby introduces the mechanism or arrangement through which something happens.

items.pt: concebido inicialmente; formulado na origem
items.example: The pilot study was initially conceived as a small-scale feasibility assessment.
items.note: Appears in the unit’s academic rewriting exercise; a natural passive research-writing collocation.

units.title: Unit 80 — Academic writing: text structure
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 80. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
units.category: Academic writing · organisation, cohesion and argumentation
learningObjectives: Emphasise, qualify and exemplify claims using precise academic reporting verbs.
Describe how information is classified and included using correct verb patterns.
Guide the reader through a discussion using conventional structural signposts.
Distinguish brief reference from thorough treatment and mark the limits of a text’s scope.

sectionsChecked: B · Categorising and including; Common mistakes: consist of
Exercises 80.1–80.4 and the corresponding answer key

items.pt: reiterar; repetir para reforçar um ponto
items.example: The authors reiterate that the findings should not be generalised beyond the study population.
items.note: Repeat a point deliberately to emphasise it; more formal than say again.

items.pt: resumir; apresentar os pontos principais de forma concisa
items.example: The discussion section summarises the limitations before outlining future work.
items.note: Present the main points rather than repeat all details; British spelling.

items.pt: exemplificar perfeitamente; representar de modo exemplar
items.example: The dispute epitomises the difficulties of introducing a policy without public consultation.
items.note: An example which captures the characteristic essence of a wider problem or attitude.

items.pt: afirmar categoricamente; sustentar com convicção
items.example: The article asserts that institutional trust is the decisive factor in compliance.
items.note: Assert a claim confidently; the verb itself does not establish that the claim is true.

items.pt: expor detalhadamente; desenvolver uma teoria ou ideia
items.example: The philosopher expounded her theory in a series of lectures.
items.note: Expound an idea or expound on a topic means explain it in a detailed, systematic way.

items.pt: ressaltar; enfatizar a importância de
items.example: The audit results underscore the need for independent verification.
items.note: A formal verb meaning emphasise or highlight significance; especially common in academic prose.

items.pt: postular; propor uma hipótese ou princípio
items.example: The framework posits a relationship between organisational culture and innovation.
items.note: Posit an explanation or link as a proposition for consideration, not necessarily an established fact.

items.pt: explicar; justificar a causa de
items.example: Variation in sample preparation may account for the discrepancies in the results.
items.note: Account for a difference or trend explains why it occurs; also has a separate quantitative meaning.

items.pt: reiterar uma preocupação
items.example: The review committee reiterated its concern about the absence of control measurements.
items.note: A standard formal collocation for restating an existing concern.

items.pt: ressaltar a importância de
items.example: These findings underscore the importance of publishing complete experimental protocols.
items.note: More precise than a generic claim that something matters; often followed by a noun or -ing form.

items.pt: postular uma ligação entre
items.example: The paper posits a link between sustained attention and long-term retention.
items.note: Use between when naming the two phenomena linked by a proposed relationship.
items.speechText: posit a link between attention and memory

items.pt: compreender; incluir como partes integrantes
items.example: Three separate investigations comprise the final phase of the programme.
items.note: Active usage can describe what makes up a whole, or the components a whole contains. Never write comprise of.

items.pt: ser composto de; consistir em
items.example: The review panel is comprised of researchers from four institutions.
items.note: The source presents be comprised of for indicating component parts; also consider comprise or consist of for formal clarity.

items.pt: consistir em; ser formado por
items.example: The evaluation consists of two surveys and a follow-up interview.
items.note: Consist must take of when introducing the component parts; do not write consist in or consist on.

items.pt: incluir como caso particular ou categoria dentro de algo mais amplo
items.example: Several minor categories can be subsumed under the heading of administrative costs.
items.note: A technical, formal verb for grouping detailed cases into a broader category.

items.pt: abranger; englobar uma variedade de temas ou aspectos
items.example: The handbook embraces legal, technical and ethical aspects of the proposed regulation.
items.note: Here embrace means include or encompass several issues, not physically hold someone.

items.pt: categorizar; classificar em grupos ou tipos
items.example: The researchers categorised the interview responses by topic and severity.
items.note: Often followed by by when indicating the classification criterion; British spelling.

items.pt: classificado por tema; categorizado por assunto
items.example: The documents were categorised by topic to facilitate comparison across departments.
items.note: Exercise-reviewed example of how to specify the basis of a classification.

items.pt: ser composto por; ser constituído de
items.example: The consortium is composed of five universities and two research institutes.
items.note: An explicit equivalent mentioned alongside be comprised of; passive be composed of is standard.

items.pt: introduzir um argumento com; fazer uma introdução antes do argumento
items.example: I shall preface my argument with a brief account of the policy’s historical context.
items.note: Preface is commonly followed by an object plus with; the introductory material comes first.
items.speechText: preface the argument with an example

items.pt: retomar esse ponto; voltar a esse argumento
items.example: I shall return to this point after examining the evidence from the second experiment.
items.note: A signposting expression that promises to revisit a topic later.

items.pt: isso me leva a; com isso passo a
items.example: This brings me to the question of how the results should be interpreted.
items.note: Connects the previous discussion to the next topic; this brings us to also works.
items.speechText: this brings me to the next question

items.pt: abordar a questão de; tratar do tema de
items.example: The next section addresses the question of whether the improvement persists over time.
items.note: Academic address means discuss or examine, not necessarily resolve a question.

items.pt: em ordem crescente
items.example: The samples are listed in ascending order of concentration.
items.note: Moves from smaller or less important values towards larger or more important ones.

items.pt: em ordem decrescente
items.example: The risks are discussed in descending order of severity.
items.note: Moves from larger or more important values towards smaller or less important ones.

items.pt: citar como sustentação de; citar para fundamentar
items.example: The author cites three longitudinal studies in support of the central claim.
items.note: Cite evidence in support of a claim; cite is not a synonym for prove.
items.speechText: cite evidence in support of the claim

items.pt: aludir a; fazer referência indireta a
items.example: The introduction alludes to earlier objections without examining them in detail.
items.note: Allude to means refer indirectly or briefly; it always takes to.

items.pt: mencionar brevemente; tratar superficialmente de
items.example: The chapter touches upon funding arrangements but focuses primarily on governance.
items.note: Use touch upon for brief treatment, as distinct from an extended analysis.

items.pt: tratar de; abordar de forma efetiva
items.example: The final part of the report deals with the ethical consequences of automated decisions.
items.note: Can mean examine a topic or handle a problem; more substantial than merely touch upon.

items.pt: fora do escopo de; além dos limites de
items.example: A full cost-benefit analysis lies beyond the scope of the present article.
items.note: A conventional way to exclude a topic while acknowledging it may be relevant.
items.speechText: beyond the scope of this article

items.pt: ser levado a concluir; não ter alternativa senão concluir
items.example: On the available evidence, we are forced to conclude that the hypothesis remains unconfirmed.
items.note: Signals a conclusion strongly compelled by the evidence or argument.
items.speechText: forced to conclude that the claim is false

items.pt: fazer alusão a um tema
items.example: Throughout the novel, the narrator alludes to themes of social exclusion and identity.
items.note: Common collocation in textual analysis, where the allusion may be indirect.

items.word: deal with a range of issues
items.pt: abordar uma variedade de questões
items.example: The review deals with a range of issues raised during the consultation.
items.note: The exercise applies deal with when indicating the breadth of a discussion.
